title: PRO Services Dubai Cost 2026: What You'll Actually Pay
description: See real 2026 PRO services cost in Dubai—monthly retainers, per-transaction fees, hidden charges, and how to pick the right provider.

contentHtml:
PRO services in Dubai usually cost AED 1,000 to AED 5,000 per month for small and medium-sized businesses, whereas larger or more complex corporate arrangements can reach AED 8,000 to AED 35,000 or more per month. Per-transaction PRO fees can range between 200 and 2,000 dirhams, depending on the task, with government fees charged separately in many cases.

The interesting part is that there is no single PRO services Dubai cost. Your final invoice depends on the number of employees, the type of government transactions, whether your company is mainland or free zone, and whether your provider charges a monthly retainer or per transaction. Government charges also vary by service and company classification, so they also need to be considered.

What Determines PRO Services Cost in Dubai

The following factors determine how much PRO services cost in Dubai:

  • Amount & type of government paperwork your company requires
  • Your number of employees
  • Jurisdiction
  • Pricing model of the PRO service provider
  • Outsourcing PRO responsibilities vs. handling it in-house.

Company Size and Employee Count

The more employees you have, the more government transactions you need a PRO to handle. Examples of required paperwork include:

  • visa applications
  • work permits
  • Emirates ID processing
  • Renewals
  • Cancellations
  • labour-related submissions
  • employee documentation

If you are a small company with 5 employees, you will need occasional PRO support at most. But if you are operating a business with 50 employees, you might have several visa and employment-related transactions every month.

Mainland vs Free Zone

Due to operating under different authorities and following different procedures, mainland and free zone businesses can face varying PRO costs.

A mainland company has to work with various regulatory authorities such as Dubai Economy and Tourism (DET), MOHRE (Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation) and GDRFA (General Directorate of Identity and Foreigners Affairs).

On the other hand, a free zone company works under its free zone authority for many licensing and employment matters.

Monthly Retainer vs Per-Transaction Pricing

PRO service providers either charge a monthly retainer or a per-transaction fee.

Retainers are great for when you have regular government paperwork. But if you only need support occasionally, per-transaction pricing is more effective.

In-House PRO vs Outsourced PRO

You can outsource PRO services or have them in-house.

When you hire an in-house PRO, you get a dedicated employee working only for you. However, the costs include salary and other employment-related costs regardless of how much government paperwork there is to handle.

According to market estimates, an in-house PRO salary is around AED 4,000 to AED 8,000 per month, before considering benefits, recruitment, leave, insurance, and other employment costs.

When you outsource, you only pay for a defined service instead.

For a small or growing company, outsourcing can be more economical.

Larger companies with constant government transactions will eventually find an internal PRO team more financially efficient.

PRO Services Cost Breakdown for 2026

PRO service cost Dubai fall into two major categories:

01. Monthly Retainer Packages

Monthly PRO retainers are for businesses that need recurring support. The exact package depends on the number of employees and transactions included.

Small Business

Small businesses, with 1 to 10 employees, can expect to pay around AED 1,000 to AED 5,000 per month for outsourced PRO support.

A basic package offered by PRO services for small businesses will include:

  • Routine government submissions
  • Visa and work permit assistance
  • Trade license renewal coordination
  • Establishment-related paperwork
  • Document clearing
  • Application tracking
  • Government correspondence and follow-up

Medium Business (10–50 Employees)

A business with 10 to 50 employees might have to pay approximately AED 2,500 to AED 8,000 or more per month, depending on transaction volume and the scope of support.

At this stage, businesses need more frequent visa processing, employee renewals, cancellations, labour-related submissions, license work, and compliance tracking.

A higher retainer can replace dozens of individual service charges throughout the year.

Corporate Retainers

Large companies can spend AED 8,000 to AED 35,000+ per month on PRO and government-relations support, especially when they have a large workforce, multiple licenses, multiple entities, or high transaction volumes.

Corporate retainers include dedicated account management, frequent employee processing, license management, immigration support, document clearing, and compliance coordination.

Per-Transaction Pricing

Per-transaction pricing works well when your company only needs PRO assistance occasionally.

Providers charge a separate service fee for each application, while government charges are added to the invoice.

Visa Processing Cost

PRO service charges for visa processing can vary considerably depending on the type of visa and whether the provider is quoting only its handling fee or an all-inclusive amount.

Market estimates put the total cost of a new employment visa process, including government and related charges, at roughly AED 2,500 to AED 7,000, although the actual amount depends on the employee's circumstances and company classification.

For example, MOHRE states that issuing or renewing a work permit can cost AED 250 to AED 3,450, depending on the company's classification.

Dubai's GDRFA separately lists an AED 200 residence permit fee, plus relevant knowledge, innovation, delivery, and in-country charges for private-sector residence permits.

Trade License Renewal Cost

The underlying government charge depends on the business activity, license structure, authority, and jurisdiction, while the PRO provider may add a separate handling fee.

Market estimates place complete mainland license renewal-related costs in the AED 5,000 to AED 15,000 range.

Your quote should distinguish between:

  • Government license renewal fees
  • PRO handling fees
  • Typing or service-center charges
  • Any applicable inspection or administrative fees
  • VAT

Document Attestation Cost

Document attestation can cost approximately AED 150 to AED 500 per document when PRO or document-clearing service charges are included, depending on the document and required attestation chain.

The underlying government, embassy, courier, and foreign-authority charges can vary. Ask whether your provider's quote covers only document handling or the entire attestation process.

Establishment Card Cost

Establishment card costs depend on the relevant authority and company structure. ICP's current establishment card service lists components including an AED 100 application fee, AED 100 annual issuance fee, AED 100 smart-services fee, and a separate AED 2,000 subscription to the authority's electronic system for establishments. Applicability can vary by establishment category and authority.

A PRO provider may also charge a separate handling fee for preparing and submitting the application.

Hidden Fees You Need to Watch Out for

You should watch out for these hidden fees being added to your total Dubai PRO service cost:

  • Government fees added after the quoted PRO fee
  • Typing-center charges
  • Medical fitness fees
  • Emirates ID fees
  • Courier or delivery charges
  • Urgent or same-day processing fees
  • Additional employee charges
  • Transactions outside the monthly package
  • Free zone authority charges
  • Document collection fees
  • Cancellation or amendment fees
  • VAT

Benefits of Using a PRO Service

A PRO service can take recurring government paperwork off your internal team's workload and assist in making certain that applications are prepared and submitted correctly.

When your company handles frequent employee, licensing, immigration, and document-related transactions, PRO services are of a greater value.

Compliance and Penalty Avoidance

A professional PRO service keeps track of government submissions, renewals, employee documentation, and deadlines, which can reduce the risk of missed renewals and incomplete applications and avoidable administrative penalties.

For example, MOHRE's work-permit system links company classification to compliance with labour laws, the Wage Protection System, and relevant ministry requirements.

However, a PRO cannot guarantee that your business will never receive a fine. But it can help prevent administrative oversights from snowballing into compliance issues.

Time Savings and Faster Processing

Government transactions require forms, supporting documents, approvals, payments, and follow-ups.

A PRO handles much of this administrative work on your behalf. This saves your teams' time and assists in documents getting processed much faster.

Government Relationship Access

Experienced PRO professionals understand what each government department and authority requires. They know which documents are requested, how applications are submitted, and where follow-up will be required. This saves you from a lot of back-and-forth.

Scalability as You Hire

Your PRO workload usually grows with your workforce. Every new employee can create additional work around permits, visas, Emirates ID, onboarding documents, renewals, and eventual cancellations. An outsourced PRO provider can increase support as your headcount grows.

Why PRO Services Matter for UAE Businesses

As a business, you have to keep up with labour, immigration, licensing, identity, and other government procedures that can involve different authorities. Keeping up with it can be stressful and can result in administrative oversight and compliance issues. That's why PRO services are important when you are running a UAE company.

Regulatory Authorities in Dubai

Dubai businesses work under several government entities depending on their activities and company structure:

  • MOHRE for major private-sector labour matters
  • GDRFA Dubai for immigration and residency services in Dubai
  • ICP for federal identity, citizenship, residency, and establishment services
  • DED regulates and licenses mainland activities

A single employee-related process can involve multiple stages across different systems. That's one reason companies use a PRO instead of assigning every government transaction to HR.

Cost of Non-Compliance

Non-compliance can result in fines, rejected applications, delayed employee processing, blocked transactions, or restrictions affecting the company's ability to complete certain government procedures.

The consequences depend on the specific violation. For example, ICP imposes an AED 2,000 fine for certain establishment-related violations and an AED 20,000 fine where entry permits are issued for an establishment that is not conducting business activity.

The cost of fixing a problem includes additional service charges, delayed onboarding, operational disruption, and employee frustration.

Emiratisation and Corporate Tax Compliance

PRO support can contribute to compliance management, especially where employee records, work permits, company classification, and Emiratisation-related requirements overlap.

However, businesses should understand the limits of a PRO service. MOHRE handles Emiratisation-related employment requirements, whereas corporate tax compliance falls under the Federal Tax Authority. So while a PRO might coordinate documents or government procedures that support compliance, that does not automatically make the provider a corporate tax adviser.

How to Choose the Right PRO Service Provider

To evaluate PRO services cost in Dubai, compare what each service provider actually handles, what's included in their retainer, and which government charges remain separate.

Verify Authorization (AMER/Tasheel Access)

Ask how the provider processes immigration and labour transactions and if the relevant applications are submitted through authorized channels. (For Dubai immigration matters, AMER service centers are official service channels referenced by GDRFA.)

For labour-related procedures, ask if the provider has access to Tasheel-related transactions.

Check Experience and Track Record

You can verify the experience and track record of a PRO service provider by asking them about the following factors:

  • Years providing PRO services
  • Industries served
  • Mainland and free zone experience
  • Client size
  • Employee visa volume
  • License renewal experience
  • Immigration and labour processing capabilities

Confirm Pricing Transparency

Request an itemized quote before signing a contract.

Your quote should distinguish between service fees and government or third-party charges. This will also help you confirm that there are no hidden markup clauses in the contract.

Also ask the service provider these questions:

  • How many transactions are included?
  • Are additional employees charged separately?
  • Are urgent applications charged extra?
  • Are government fees passed through at cost?
  • Is VAT included?
  • Are license renewals included?
  • Are visa cancellations included?
  • Are free zone charges included?
  • What happens when a transaction falls outside the package?

Match Specialization to Your Business Type

Choose a PRO provider familiar with your specific jurisdiction.

Mainland companies, free zone companies, branches, and businesses with multiple entities have different procedures and documentation requirements. A provider that mainly handles one free zone might not be the right fit for a mainland business with frequent MOHRE and GDRFA transactions.

Red Flags to Avoid

Be cautious if a provider:

  • gives you a suspiciously low quote without explaining exclusions
  • refuses to provide an itemized breakdown
  • promises guaranteed government approval
  • cannot explain which authority handles your application
  • charges unexplained 'government fees'
  • uses vague terms such as 'unlimited' without defining the scope
  • has no written service-level expectations
  • requests payments without proper invoices or receipts

FAQs

How much do PRO services cost in Dubai per month?

PRO services in Dubai cost AED 1,000 to AED 5,000 per month for many SMEs. Larger companies with higher transaction volumes might pay AED 8,000 to AED 35,000 or more.

What is included in a PRO services retainer?

A PRO services retainer usually covers recurring government liaison and administrative support, such as visa processing, work permit assistance, license renewal coordination, document submissions, application tracking, and government follow-up.

Is it cheaper to hire an in-house PRO or outsource?

For small and medium-sized businesses, it is cheaper to outsource PRO services. For larger companies with frequent government transactions and a constant administrative workload, it is cheaper to have an in-house PRO.

Do PRO service costs differ between free zone and mainland companies?

Yes, PRO service costs can differ between free zone and mainland companies because of different authorities, systems, licensing requirements, and employment procedures.

What hidden fees should I watch for with PRO service providers?

You should watch out for government charges, typing-center fees, medical testing, Emirates ID charges, courier fees, urgent processing fees, extra employee charges, and transactions outside a monthly package.

How much does visa processing cost through a PRO service?

Visa processing cost through a PRO service includes government and related charges along with the PRO's own fee which itself is usually lower than the actual cost. The government charges for visa processing can cost between 2,500 to 7,000 dirhams per employee, MOHRE's work permit fees alone range from AED 250 to AED 3,450 depending on company classification, and GDRFA separately lists residence permit charges for private-sector employees.

How do I choose a reliable PRO service company in Dubai?

To choose a reliable PRO service company in Dubai, look for their proven experience with your business structure. Verify if it uses authorised government channels, provides itemised pricing, and clearly explains which services and government fees are included. You should also ask them about how they handle additional or urgent transactions.
